name: Audit the Plan
brief:
Somebody built this network from a written plan and got three things wrong. The plan is correct; the network does not match it.

  LAN-A  192.168.50.0/26    gateway .1     PC-A .10
  LAN-B  192.168.50.64/27   gateway .65    PC-B .70
  LAN-C  192.168.50.96/28   gateway .97    PC-C .100, SRV .110
  WAN    192.168.50.112/30  R1 .113, R2 .114

Find all three violations and fix them. Nothing here needs a new route — every fault is an addressing fault.
watchFor: A subnet has three addresses you can never give a host: the network address, the broadcast address, and anything outside the block. At least one of these three faults is one of those.

tasks.text: Start with ipconfig on each PC and show ip interface brief on each router. Write down what you see before you change anything.
Fault one: PC-B is not on LAN-B at all. Put it back at 192.168.50.70/27.
tasks.hint: .96 is the network address of LAN-C. It is not a host address anywhere, and it is nowhere near LAN-B.

tasks.text: Fault two: R2 GigabitEthernet0/1 carries the wrong mask. LAN-C is a /28.
tasks.hint: A /24 there swallows every other subnet in the plan, so R2 starts sending LAN-A traffic out of its own LAN port.

tasks.text: Fault three: PC-C is pointed at the wrong gateway. LAN-C's gateway is .97.
tasks.hint: .65 is LAN-B's router. It is not on PC-C's subnet, so PC-C cannot even ARP for it.

tasks.text: Prove PC-B can reach the server at 192.168.50.110.
Prove it works in the other direction too: PC-C can reach PC-A.

extension: The server sits at 192.168.50.110. Is that the last usable address on LAN-C, or the broadcast? Prove your answer from the mask rather than from the fact that it works.
debrief:
Three faults, three different symptoms, and none of them mention a mask or a boundary in the error text. A host with an address outside its own subnet cannot reach its gateway. A router with too wide a mask claims networks that are not on that wire. A host with a gateway on somebody else's subnet ARPs into the void.

All three are found the same way: read the address and the mask together, work out the subnet, and compare it to the plan. That is the whole skill.
